request: I run a small provisions shop in Madina and I want to keep my price list on the computer instead of in my notebook. I want to add the things I sell with their prices. I want to see everything I sell, and look up the price of one thing. Sometimes I stop selling something, so I want to take it off the list.
summary:
I've built your price list program. It saves everything in a file called `shop.db` in the same folder, so your list is still there after you close it and open it again. I wrote 6 automatic checks covering adding, viewing, looking up, removing and refusing bad entries, and they all pass.

**What it can do:**
- **Add an item:** you give it a name and a price, for example "Rice 5kg" at 85.50. The program gives each item a number (an ID), which you use to look it up or remove it later.
- **See everything you sell:** shows the full list in A–Z order by name.
- **Look up one item's price:** you look it up by its ID number.
- **Take an item off the list:** you remove it by its ID number.

**Things it will refuse:**
- A price below zero.
- An item with no name, or no price.
- An item that's already on the list. Capital letters don't matter here, so "Bread" and "bread" count as the same thing. You didn't ask for this; I added it so the same item can't end up on the list twice with two prices.
- Looking up or removing an item that isn't on the list (it says "Item not found").

**Things you didn't ask for, so I left them out:**
- **Changing a price:** there's no way to edit a price yet. To change one, you'd have to remove the item and add it again.
- **Looking up by name:** you need the item's ID number, not its name. I can add a name search if that would be easier.

These are the actions behind the scenes, in case someone sets this up for you:
- `POST /items` adds an item
- `GET /items` shows the full list
- `GET /items/{id}` looks up one item
- `DELETE /items/{id}` removes an item
